title: Reversible and irreversible sorting cards
subject: Science
unit: Spring 2: Changes of materials and animals including humans
source: Seeded from science/y5 lesson 21 (Reversible and irreversible sorting cards (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 21: Irreversible changes: making new materials. To understand that some changes make new materials and cannot be undone

cards:
irreversible
a change that cannot be undone

new material
a different substance made in
a change

reaction
a change where new materials
are made

carbon dioxide
a gas made when vinegar and
bicarbonate of soda mix
blocks.task: use them to test yourself or a partner.

questions.q: Is toasting bread reversible or irreversible? Why?
questions.a: Irreversible: the toast is a new material; you cannot make it bread again
questions.model: Can I get the bread back? No. Is something new made? Yes: brown, crunchy toast. So it is irreversible.

questions.q: What gas is made when vinegar and bicarbonate of soda mix?
Give one sign that a new material has formed.
questions.a: For example: fizzing, colour change, heat

questions.q: Put one teaspoon of bicarbonate of soda in a balloon. Stretch it over a small bottle with 3 cm of vinegar and tip the powder in (adult present). Record what you see.
questions.a: Fizzing in the bottle; the balloon inflates with carbon dioxide; a new material is made
questions.model: Teacher does it on camera first and names the signs: 'Fizzing, the balloon grows: a gas is made.'

questions.q: Sort these changes: melting ice, baking bread, dissolving salt, rusting nail, freezing juice, burning wood.
questions.a: Reversible: melting ice, dissolving salt, freezing juice. Irreversible: baking bread, rusting nail, burning wood

questions.q: Why is it not possible to get the vinegar and bicarbonate back?
questions.a: They reacted to make new materials (carbon dioxide, water and a salt).

questions.q: Big question: can you unbake a cake?
questions.a: No: baking makes new materials, so it is irreversible.
